title: Expectation stability under uniform approximation
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $f,g\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with $f$ integrable and $g$ measurable up to a null set. If $D\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $|f(\omega)-g(\omega)|\le D$ for every $\omega\in\Omega$, then $\left|\int f\,d\mu-\int g\,d\mu\right|\le D$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is measurable up to a null set
replaced: Let $f,g\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, with $f$ integrable and $g$ measurable up to a null set. If a real constant $D$ satisfies $|f(\omega)-g(\omega)|\le D$ for every $\omega$, then $|\int f\,d\mu-\int g\,d\mu|\le D$.
